title: Implemented the Growth Data API and the growth change log
reason: Expose decision-quality, aggregated growth data (traffic, funnel, commercial, first-touch and last-touch attribution, content-level UTM breakdowns) to an external growth agent, and give it a record of growth-relevant product changes to read alongside the numbers
author: claude-code
notes: Read-only. Own bearer token GROWTH_AGENT_TOKEN (503 until set on the server). No public page, copy, price or tracking change; visitor-facing behaviour is unchanged, so no metric is expected to move.

title: Collapsed the www + legacy-article redirect chain to one hop and made /llms.txt discoverable
reason: A traffic and SEO audit on 2026-09-22 found that the URL Google actually has indexed for the best-performing article is https://www.drawreport.com/blog/<old>.html, and that it cost TWO 301s to reach the live page: nginx sent www to the apex keeping the path, then the app sent the legacy path to /en/blog/<slug>. Legacy .html URLs carried 36 of 163 engaged human visits (22%) in the 36 days of analytics that exist, so this is the live entry path for roughly a fifth of real traffic, not a tidy-up. Real Googlebot crawls this site about 9 times a day and spent 21 of 132 hits on redirects. Separately, /llms.txt had nothing pointing at it and llmstxt.org specifies no discovery mechanism: in 14 days ClaudeBot made 185 requests, ChatGPT-User 162, OAI-SearchBot 49 and GPTBot 39, and none of them fetched it, while chatgpt.com was the best-converting source in the dataset (6 engaged visits, 1 free upload, 1 completion).
affected_area: drawreportDeploy/nginx-drawreport-tls.conf (www block: proxy / and /blog*, catch-all redirect moved into location /)
app/__init__.py (root redirect now absolute on PUBLIC_BASE_URL)
templates/_verification.html (<link rel=alternate> to /llms.txt on both page frames)
author: claude-code
notes: No visible copy, price or layout change - a visitor sees the same pages. The expected effect is on how fast Google consolidates the legacy URLs onto the /en/blog/ ones and on crawl budget, which is slow and confounded by an ad that stopped mid-window; do not read a week-on-week organic move as caused by this alone. Deliberately NOT bumping SITEMAP_LASTMOD: nothing a reader sees changed, and a lastmod that moves for an invisible head tag is the same lie V0.043 removed.

title: Fixed three robots.txt Disallow rules that matched no live URL
reason: robots.txt matches a path prefix from the root of the site, but the main blueprint is mounted at /<lang_code>, so the live URLs are /en/cabinet, /en/order and /en/r/<token>. The rules read /cabinet, /order and /r/ and therefore matched nothing at all - three of the five rules had never done anything, and only /admin and /free, whose blueprints really do sit at the root, worked. Found while auditing crawl budget on 2026-09-22: in 14 days of logs bingbot, GPTBot, Amazonbot, AhrefsBot and Bytespider all fetched /en/login and /en/order. Nothing was ever exposed - every one of those pages carries its own noindex, nofollow and that is what kept them out of the index - but a Disallow prevents the fetch where noindex only discards it afterwards, and real Googlebot only crawls this site about 9 times a day. /en/login is linked from the header of every page, which makes it the most crawlable dead end on the site.
affected_area: app/routes.py (SEO_DISALLOW split into SEO_DISALLOW_ROOT + SEO_DISALLOW_LOCALE, expanded per locale by seo_disallow())
author: claude-code
notes: No visitor-facing change and no metric is expected to move on its own; the effect is that crawl budget goes to pages that can rank instead of to the login and checkout screens. /login and /pay/ were added to the list for the same reason. Verified that no disallowed path is in the sitemap and that /en/report, /en/, the articles and the sample pages are all still crawlable.

title: No visit row for a request on a non-canonical host (www)
reason: Prerequisite for the one-hop www change in DR-CHG-0002. Once nginx hands the app '/' and '/blog...' on www.drawreport.com instead of redirecting them itself, a non-canonical host reaches app/track.py for the first time. The visit row it would create can never be completed: the cookie is set on www.drawreport.com and the browser's next request goes to drawreport.com, and a cookie does not cross hosts. Every www arrival would therefore book TWO visits - one dead row that can never record a page or an engagement, plus the real one - inflating visits_raw, visits_non_bot and visitors_unique_non_bot. This is the same failure as the uptime monitor that used to invent ~288 visits a day, reached by a different road.
author: claude-code
notes: Shipped BEFORE the nginx change so the app is safe whenever that is applied; on its own it changes nothing, because today nginx redirects www and no www request ever reaches the app. visits_engaged_human, the primary metric, was never at risk either way - a 301 runs no JavaScript, so a phantom row could not be engaged. Counted here as a prevented inflation, not a correction: no historical number is affected.

title: Owner requested indexing in Search Console for the three legacy-traffic articles
reason: Google is the one engine still serving the pre-i18n /blog/<old>.html URLs and it does not take part in IndexNow, so a manual Request indexing in Search Console is the only lever that exists. Done by the owner on 2026-09-22 for /en/blog/kids-drawings-missing-body-parts-meaning, /en/blog/my-child-only-draws-in-black and /en/blog/child-draws-alone-figures-meaning - the three articles carrying the legacy traffic. Pairs with DR-CHG-0002, which cut the www redirect chain for those same URLs from two hops to one.
affected_area: Google Search Console (URL Inspection -> Request indexing)
author: owner
notes: BASELINE captured the same day, measured from entry_path on engaged human visits (analytics starts 2026-08-17): across the three articles, 36 arrivals landed on the legacy .html URL and 32 on the new /en/blog/ one - a legacy share of 53 percent. Google already serves BOTH forms, so this is a partial consolidation being finished, not a migration that never started. Per article: missing-body-parts 24 legacy / 14 new, only-in-black 9 / 15, draws-alone 3 / 3. Google-referred engaged humans overall: 35 legacy landings, 42 new. SUCCESS = legacy share trending to zero; it does NOT require organic volume to rise. Do not read a change before mid-October: real Googlebot hits this site about 9 times a day, and the window is confounded by a Facebook ad that stopped mid-September.

title: form_started now reaches the paid funnel (marker mismatch fixed)
reason: The 2026-09-25 technical sanity check found the order form sent form_started as a raw sendBeacon with no page path; /t/e stores every g= beacon as click:<goal>, so it was stored as click:form_started with path NULL, while app/admin_funnels.py PAID_STEPS matched the literal 'form_started', a name nothing ever stored. 'Started filling it in' was therefore always 0 (6 visits opened the form, 0 'started'): an artifact, not behaviour.
affected_area: static/js/order.js (drGoal('form_started') on first input/change, once per page load)
author: claude-code
notes: Historical rows were stored as click:form_started all along, so with the corrected marker the step is recounted retroactively from real events; nothing was backfilled or invented. Rows written before V0.078 carry path NULL. The goal now also reaches GA4 and the Meta Pixel as form_started (custom event) because it goes through drGoal.

title: Order form ported to the design-system form styling
reason: /en/order rendered as raw browser controls on every device: its markup used class names (form-row, draw-block, is-hidden, field-err, ym) that no stylesheet ever defined. Consequences: all three drawing blocks always visible, 13px inputs (iOS zooms on every tap), validation errors indistinguishable from hints.
affected_area: static/js/order.js (new: add/remove drawing, preview, double-submit guard)
author: claude-code
notes: No field name, validation rule, price or copy change. Before/after is confounded by the other V0.078 changes and by near-zero paid traffic (0 orders ever); do not attribute a conversion change to this entry alone.

title: Free -> paid handoff: order form continues the free reading (prefill + reused drawing)
reason: The free result CTA promised 'The drawing is already uploaded - you won't need to add it again', but /en/order arrived completely empty. Now, for the browser that uploaded the free drawing and for a finished ('done') reading only: child name, pronoun (she/he -> girl/boy) and email are prefilled, and the free drawing is attached server-side as drawing 1 with an inline thumbnail. Birth month/year, drawing date and subject stay manual (the wizard only knows an age band).
author: claude-code
notes: Attribution (orders.free_token) is kept and now also set when the reading was opened on another device, but only if the token names an existing reading. New server event order_form_from_free when a handoff renders; order_created payload gains free_drawing_reused.

title: Free-reading token no longer reaches GA4 or Meta; GA4 removed from private pages
reason: The free-reading token (the only key to a child's drawing page) was sent to Meta and GA4 as the page URL of /en/order?free=<token>, and to GA4 on /free/r/<token>. Now: the token travels in an httponly first-party cookie (legacy ?free= links are moved into it by a server redirect before any page renders); GA4, like the pixel already, is not rendered on /free/r/, /<lang>/r/ or the cabinet; the order page continuing a free reading loads neither tag; /free/r/*, /free/to-order/*, /free/img/* and /free/status/* send Referrer-Policy: no-referrer.
author: claude-code
notes: Visible effect on third-party dashboards: GA4 loses page_view and events on /free/r/* and hosted reports, and neither GA4 nor Meta sees the order page or order_pay/form_started for visitors arriving from a free reading. First-party analytics (track.js, the Growth API) is unaffected and still sees all of it. Privacy Policy wording already promised this for the pixel; GA4 is not named in the policy (pre-existing gap, flagged for the owner).

title: Meta Lead (free_upload_submit) fires only on an accepted upload
reason: free_upload_submit was a data-goal click attribute and fired on every press of 'Get my reading', including presses the form then rejected (no email, no file); it maps to the Meta standard event Lead. The sanity-check upload produced 2 Leads for 1 upload. It is now fired from static/js/free.js only after POST /free/upload/<token> returns 200 ok; the server refuses a second upload for the same token, so 1 accepted upload = at most 1 Lead.
author: claude-code
notes: Break in series: from V0.078 click:free_upload_submit / Lead count ACCEPTED uploads, before it counted button presses. Do not compare Lead or cost-per-lead across 2026-09-25. The server event free_upload was always correct and is unchanged.
